claims.text: HfZrTiTa0.53 has a reported yield strength of 786 MPa.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has a reported compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has a reported terminal strain of 13.5%.
The reported 13.5% terminal strain represents the alloy's baseline tensile uniform elongation.
The proposed intervention is controlled cold work followed by a subtransus isothermal anneal.
The proposed processing will produce fine recrystallized grains along grain boundaries within a coarser matrix.
The processing will increase the prevalence of stable fine-grained boundaries without deleterious grain growth.
A refined bimodal grain structure will delay tensile strain localization and promote more homogeneous deformation.
The refined bimodal grain structure will enhance or optimize grain-boundary sliding.
Delayed localization and enhanced grain-boundary sliding will increase tensile uniform elongation.
The processed alloy's overall phase distribution will preserve its yield and compressive strengths.
The processed alloy's overall phase distribution will preserve impact-triggered chemical-energy release.
Processing will increase tensile uniform elongation from the asserted 13.5% baseline to approximately 20% or more.
Processing will maintain yield strength near 786 MPa.
Processing will maintain compressive strength around 1314 MPa.
Processing will sustain impact-triggered chemical-energy release comparable to the baseline.
The hypothesized tensile benefit applies at room temperature under tensile loading at a strain rate near 10^-3 s^-1.
Extreme strain rates or temperatures above approximately 0.5 of the melting temperature may cause microstructural changes or grain coarsening that negate the ductility improvement.
The hypothesis is falsified if processed specimens achieve less than a statistically significant 15% relative increase in tensile uniform elongation over the baseline.
The hypothesis is also falsified if processing significantly reduces yield strength, compressive strength, or impact-triggered energy release relative to the baseline.

contradictions.description: The 13.5% value is called terminal strain in one field but is treated as tensile uniform elongation in other fields. Terminal strain and uniform elongation are not established as equivalent here.
